record.paper_title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials
record.context_brief: Eventual vanishing of Delta^m P^m versus Hessian nilpotency
record.original_question: Let P(z) be a formal power series in C[[z]] with order o(P(z)) at least 2, and let Delta be the Laplace operator. If the sequence Delta^m(P(z)^m) eventually vanishes, meaning Delta^m(P(z)^m) = 0 for all sufficiently large m, must P(z) be Hessian nilpotent?

evidence.quote: A polynomial or formal power series P (z) is said to be HN (Hessian nilpotent) if its Hessian matrix Hes P := (d^2P/dz_i dz_j) are nilpotent.
Conjecture 6.4. Let P (z) in C[[z]] with o(P (z)) >= 2. If Delta^m P^m (z) = 0 for m >> 0, then P (z) is HN.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}[[z]] = \mathbb{C}[[z_1,\dots,z_n]]$ denote the ring of formal power series in $n$ variables over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\Delta = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \partial^2/\partial z_i^2$ be the (formal) Laplace operator. For $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ with no constant or linear term (i.e. with order $o(P) \geq 2$), say that $P$ is Hessian nilpotent (HN) if its Hessian matrix $\mathrm{Hes}\, P := (\partial^2 P/\partial z_i \partial z_j)_{1\le i,j\le n}$ is a nilpotent matrix with entries in $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$.

Prove or disprove: if $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ satisfies $o(P) \geq 2$ and there exists $M \geq 1$ such that
$$\Delta^m \big(P(z)^m\big) = 0 \quad \text{for all } m \geq M,$$
then $P(z)$ must be Hessian nilpotent.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture concerning whether eventual vanishing of $\Delta^m P^m$ forces Hessian nilpotency (the known equivalence is with vanishing for all $m \geq 1$, which connects to the Jacobian conjecture via Zhao's reformulation). Searches in the literature on Hessian nilpotent polynomials and the associated vanishing conjecture turn up the standard equivalence and the Jacobian-conjecture connection, but no published proof or counterexample to the eventual-vanishing version. It appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials and the Jacobian Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The condition $\Delta^m P^m=0$ for all $m\geq 1$ is equivalent to $P$ being Hessian nilpotent; equivalence with the Jacobian conjecture is established.
status_evidence.claim: The all-$m$ vanishing version is the established equivalence; the eventual-vanishing variant is the natural strengthening posed as a conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Some properties of and open problems on Hessian nilpotent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: A list of open problems on Hessian nilpotent polynomials, including conjectures relating eventual vanishing of $\Delta^m P^m$ to Hessian nilpotency.
status_evidence.claim: The eventual-vanishing implication is listed as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A Vanishing Conjecture on Differential Operators with Constant Coefficients
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the vanishing conjectures for $\Delta^m P^m$ and related operators; treats the standard equivalence with HN polynomials and the Jacobian conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the eventual-vanishing converse is reported.
